title: Experiences in Managing High-performance Computing Management and Support Tools while Upgrading a Campus Cluster
problem: Managing the transition of a campus research computing cluster from TSCC 1.0 to TSCC 2.0 while overcoming challenges of node heterogeneity, inefficient job scheduling, and inequitable resource allocation and billing.
motivation: Campus HPC clusters require fair resource allocation and efficient scheduling mechanisms to serve diverse research workloads while maintaining operational continuity.
method: The team redesigned the cluster infrastructure to better manage different hardware types. They replaced the job scheduling system to more effectively match computing tasks with available resources. They created new billing and resource allocation rules to ensure fair distribution of computing time across different research groups.
key_novelty: The paper documents how a real research institution successfully transitioned its computing cluster to handle diverse hardware types fairly and schedule jobs more efficiently.
contributions: Analysis of TSCC 1.0 limitations and critical issues requiring resolution in campus HPC environments
Implementation strategies for HPC management tools and infrastructure upgrades in TSCC 2.0
Approaches for handling node heterogeneity and optimizing job scheduling efficiency
Best practices for fair resource allocation and billing in campus computing clusters

metrics.other: Improved job scheduling efficiency and resource allocation fairness

limitations: Specific quantitative performance metrics and comparative baselines are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: campus HPC cluster operations and management
